answer.reason: The verses tell of his pleading with the king for Jeremiah and rescuing him from the dungeon, and of the LORD's promise to deliver him.

clauses.english: pleaded with King Zedekiah for Jeremiah, who had been put in the dungeon
clauses.quote: Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon

clauses.english: drew Jeremiah up out of the dungeon with cords and rags
clauses.quote: Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords.

clauses.english: was promised deliverance by the LORD because he trusted in him
clauses.quote: I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword

doubts: The first two clauses could be read as one rescue; kept apart as the plea to the king and the lifting out of the dungeon.
